questions.section: Part One: Reading Comprehension – Nelson Mandela (20 marks) – Answer the following questions
questions.question:
Read the passage “Nelson Mandela – Background”:

Nelson Rolihlala Mandela (born 18 July 1918) served as president of South Africa from 1994 – 1999. He was the firsts South- African president to be elected in a fully representative democratic election.

Before his presidency, Mandela was anti- apartheid activist and the leader of Umkhonto We sizwe, the army wing of African national congress (ANC). He coordinated Sabotage campaigns against military and government targets making plans for a possible guirrilla war.

In 1962 he was arrested and convicted of sabotage and other charges. In his statement from courtroom at the opening of the defense case in the trail on 20 April 1964 at the Pretoria Supreme Court, Mandela laid out the reasoning in the ANC's choice to use violence as a tactic. When he gave this address it was widely thought that the judges would agree to the demands of the senior prosecutor and impose the death penalty. How over, he was sentenced to life imprisonment without release. Mandela spent 27 years in jail before he was released as part of several political reforms introduced by the white regime.

---

questions.section: PART FOUR: COMPOSITION (20marks)
questions.question:
Select one of the following topics to write composition of not less than 200 words.

1- Fishing Importance of water
   a. Importance of fishing
   b. Health benefits
   c. Economic benefits
   d. Problems face with fisher men

2- Cultivation
   a. Importance of cultivation
   b. Factors that affect with cultivation
   c. Areas of cultivation in Somaliland.
questions.answer_guide: Choose ONE topic, at least 200 words: introduction; one paragraph per guide point – (1) fishing gives food and jobs, fish is rich in protein/omega-3, earns income and exports, fishermen face poor equipment, lack of markets, illegal foreign fishing and bad weather; (2) cultivation provides food security and income, is affected by rainfall, soil, water, pests and tools, and is practised in areas such as Gabiley, Arabsiyo, Borama and Sheikh; conclusion. Marks for content, organisation, vocabulary, grammar and spelling.
